rationale: flops-5 is a tiny (791-byte text, single real function) floating-point kernel whose entire execution is a hot arithmetic loop, so passes with per-iteration overhead must be kept in check: SUB gets the highest weight because algebraic instruction substitution adds strong static diversity to dense FP/integer arithmetic at near-zero runtime cost and minimal correctness risk, while FLA and BCF are weighted moderately so they apply only where control-flow features justify it, since a dispatcher or bogus predicates inside the hot loop would directly erode the benchmark's flops rate; SPLIT and IBR provide cheap structural diversity on the limited branching present and are given mild weights; ICALL and IGV are weighted low because this program is essentially one self-contained main with few indirect-call or global-variable opportunities, so those passes would add indirection overhead without meaningful reverse-engineering payoff; all RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are kept low across the board to respect the program's compute-bound, size-trivial profile, and CorrectnessRisk weights stay low since FP-heavy arithmetic tolerates none of these transformations poorly.
